newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin pledges no rise in payroll charges.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin pledges no rise in payroll charges.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin said in a radio interview on Friday that the Socialists would not raise payroll charges if they won the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.
"I take up the pledge not to raise payroll charges, which (Prime Minister Alain) Juppe has brought to record levels," Jospin told RMC radio.
The centre-right RPR-UDF coalition says the Socialists' plan to create 700,000 jobs for young people would require tax increases.
Jospin reiterated that the Socialist plan pledges to create of 350,000 jobs in the public sector and 350,000 in the private sector over two years.
The 350,000 public sector jobs would be financed mainly from the state budget but also from regional and municipal authorities, he said. He has promised not to raise spending to create the jobs.

Jospin said the Socialists could not offer a similar guarantee on their objective to create 350,000 private sector jobs, as that would depend a great deal on corporate decisions. But he said the Socialists would try to lead them in that direction through incentive measures.
"We'll take these measures without raising charges -- that's the commitment I'm making," Jospin said.
